sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPU renderer with WebGL 2 fallback, Rapier 0.19.3, Web Audio, Gamepad API, PeerJS 1.5.4 / WebRTC, AI Hub session client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural cel-shaded / ink desert diorama, faceted vehicles, warm ochre and teal palette
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer with native keyframe clips for rotors, jet exhaust and waving pilots; procedural flight and particles
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written synth music (10% default), effects, rotor sound and Animalese-style radio gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 co-op: standalone WebRTC flight codes, same-origin BroadcastChannel fallback, AI Hub host-authoritative shared-world sessions; local second-controller co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium WebGPU; full campaign with and without invincibility; emulated standard gamepads; real browser multitouch emulation; OfflineAudioContext; file:// boot; standalone two-page co-op; AI Hub normal, host-leave and server-only scenarios at 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter and 5% loss; 1920×1080 WebGL fallback visual checks. Physical controller, real iOS device and cross-device NAT behavior: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: No internet game research; native model knowledge. Retrieved only the user-linked AI Hub integration reference and package dependencies.

testingFeedback: 5 issues caught by testing: a guest snapshot exception, three HUD contrast problems and cockpit visibility when facing left. All fixed.
1 critical issue: the guest snapshot exception interrupted co-op state updates.
The full scripted campaign through real Rapier collisions, including rescues, upgrades and the carrier; it also completed with invincibility disabled.
The first headless WebGPU screenshot was blank. State checks and WebGL fallback screenshots were useful instead.
engineFeedback: Three.js native keyframe animation and the WebGPU renderer fit the small procedural diorama well.

Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank on this machine; the native WebGL 2 fallback provided visual verification. Browser input and snapshot lifecycle mistakes were corrected during review and testing.
The arcade campaign, radar, convoy AI, controller-first menus and authoritative co-op simulation.
Keeping the simulation, browser inputs and multiplayer lifecycle synchronized.
A built-in game input and UI navigation layer with deterministic replay would reduce glue code.
promptFeedback: The specific source, controller-first requirements and complete-demo scope gave a clear design target.
The no-research rule and mandatory linked online specification require distinguishing game research from integration documentation.
Delivering the full campaign and multiplayer lifecycle in one shareable HTML file.
Specify a target campaign length and whether local co-op is required in addition to online.

aiHub.name: Chopper Palooza
aiHub.description: Fly a cel-shaded desert patrol, defend six trucks and recover downed pilots. Clear three sectors, choose field upgrades and bring down the command carrier solo or with a wingmate.
aiHub.controls: WASD / left stick fly; mouse / right stick aim; click, Space or R2 fire; Shift / L2 boost; Q / Circle flare; E / Cross rescue; Esc / Options pause.
